newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH IPB SAYS 96 LOSS RUMOURS "NONSENSE".
newsitem.headline: CZECH IPB SAYS 96 LOSS RUMOURS "NONSENSE".

text.p: The Czech Republic's third largest bank IPB a.s. on Thursday strongly denied widespread market rumours that it would post big losses for 1996 saying they were "nonsense".
Asked whether IPB would report losses on its 1996 results, IPB's Deputy for International Banking, Libor Prochazka told Reuters: "It is nonsense. I can repeat that." He declined to comment further.

IPB is due to release its results in the next few days and local share and bond dealers say rumours that it has been forced to make heavy provisions against bad loans, and that IPB would have to post big 1996 losses, have depressed prices.
Early in continuous trading on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) IPB's share price fell 25 crowns, 7.6 percent, to 305 and one local dealer said the rumours were clearly responsible for the fall.
A similar scenario emerged on the bond market.
"On Monday IPB one was quoted 99.10 to 99.30 which was a yield on the bid side at 12.23 and right now it is bidded by IPB at 98 which gives a yield of 13.27," said ABN Amro bond dealer Jan Brozik.
IPB's preliminary 1996 results according to international accounting standards showed a pre-tax profit of 1.6 billion crowns from 1.4 billion the year before.

In early March, IPB announced it was changing its auditor from Coopers & Lybrand to Ernst and Young which caused speculation that the bank was unhappy with its previous auditor's recommendations on provisioning.
